vis.alt: Baroreceptor reflex loop: raised blood pressure stretches carotid sinus and aortic arch receptors, afferents via IX and X reach the nucleus tractus solitarius, which increases vagal tone and reduces sympathetic outflow, lowering heart rate and vessel tone and so pressure.
vis.caption: Rising pressure fires baroreceptors, which brake the heart through the vagus and relax vessels; standing does the opposite.

vis.alt: Autonomic dysreflexia in spinal injury above T6: a stimulus below the lesion, usually a full bladder or bowel, causes a sympathetic surge with severe hypertension; baroreflex slows the heart but cannot relax vessels below the lesion; treat by sitting up, removing the stimulus and lowering the pressure.
vis.caption: Spinal cord injury at or above T6: noxious stimulus below the lesion leads to severe hypertension; sit up and remove the trigger.
